lessons.title: Agentic CX is a flow exit, not a magic queue
outcomes: Map every exit to a queue, a message, or a failure prompt.
Pass only the attributes the bot needs.
Keep a DTMF path to a person.
Load-test the tool. The flow timeout still exists.

lessons.title: Turn on assist only where you can show the source
outcomes: Quick responses and message templates have their own quotas.
Real-time recommendations need the analytics path enabled for that contact.
Do not paste customer secrets into a knowledge article.
Test with a question the article answers and a question it does not. The second test matters more.

lessons.title: Wisdom, Q, and agent assist are one lineage
outcomes: Connect assistant associates an AI agents domain with the contact.
Self-service with the assistant was announced 1 December 2024.
Agentic self-service, including Nova Sonic for voice, was announced 30 November 2025.
Agentic CX designer was previewed 22 June 2026 and generally available 2 September 2026.

lessons.title: Voice ID has ended
outcomes: Do not grant voiceid IAM permissions for a new design.
If you still have a domain from before the end date, follow the guide's export and delete steps. Do not assume the data remains.
Authentication for a new design is Cognito plus Profiles, or your own Lambda check.
Say 'ended' in the migration map so nobody plans a phase around it.

lessons.title: Agent events are the live staffing truth
outcomes: A missed logout event leaves someone 'available' in the third-party tool.
Status names must match the WFM map.
Do not let a test tool consume the production stream without its own iterator.
Firehose to S3 is the historical copy. The stream is the live copy.

lessons.title: Read a CTR before you build a dashboard
outcomes: DisconnectReason is the first field when someone says the carrier dropped the call.
Attributes are whatever you wrote. They are not infinite.
A missing Recording.Location means recording was off or the write failed.
Do not average a day from real-time screenshots.

lessons.title: Conversational analytics is Contact Lens under a new name
outcomes: Redaction is a setting. Confirm it before you promise it.
Categories are rules. They are not Lex intents.
Summaries can be wrong. The recording is the evidence.
A contact with analytics off produces no transcript to search.

lessons.title: Real-time boards and historical intervals
outcomes: Abandonment before the queue and abandonment in queue are different.
ACW is in occupancy. A dashboard that ignores it flatters the team.
Custom metrics exist and have a quota of 1,000.
The analytics data lake, previewed 28 November 2023, is the zero-ETL path into Athena or QuickSight.

lessons.title: The mapping table you put in the migration pack
outcomes: Write one row per old object, with the Connect object and the pitfall.
Skills can become proficiencies or extra queues. Pick one and say why.
Hunt pilots become queues plus priority and delay.
The lab translator does this row by row.

lessons.title: Pitfalls that show up in every platform
outcomes: Write the AHT formula on the report.
Test the external transfer with a real desk phone.
Inventory holidays.
Decide what 'abandoned' means.

lessons.title: A migration playbook
outcomes: Dual-run the recording tools.
Translate quick connects from the old speed-dial list, and delete the dead ones.
Hours and holidays are a data migration, not a memory test.
Keep a glossary so 'skill' means one thing in the new design.

lessons.title: CUIC and the Connect report are different clocks
outcomes: Service level target seconds must match or you publish two truths.
Transfers inflate contact counts. Deduplicate on the chain.
Outbound and inbound should not share one AHT.
The data lake is where you freeze the definition.

lessons.title: Campaigns dial only after the quota is not zero
outcomes: Raise the concurrent campaign quota before the first run.
AMD branches need a prompt for humans and a disposition for machines.
Compliance with calling hours is your job. The block will dial when the campaign says to.
Email and SMS campaigns use the message prices, not the voice minute.

lessons.title: Chat, SMS, WhatsApp, and the idle-chat quota
outcomes: StartChatContact is an API. Call it from your backend.
The same queue and routing profile can include chat with its own concurrency.
Attachments and rich messages have size limits. Email attachments are a different channel.
Alarm on concurrent chats at 80 percent.

lessons.title: Email is a contact with a 90-day thread
outcomes: Outbound email from an agent and a flow acknowledgment are both billable messages in the examples.
SES networking applies if you send a lot.
Put the case id in the thread so the next reply finds it.
Do not staff email on a voice-only routing profile.

lessons.title: In-app, web, and video
outcomes: Allow the widget origin.
Test the customer network, not only the agent's.
A video failure with working audio is a Chime path problem.
Record the fact that video was used. It changes the price and the privacy notice.

lessons.title: Twilio Flex is a different product, documented on its own site
outcomes: The Flex guide tells you to add https://flex.twilio.com as a Salesforce trusted URL.
It says an outbound call should start with the Salesforce record already open, or the activity may log on the wrong record.
If third-party cookies are blocked, that guide says to turn on Login using popup.
Draw Connect and Flex as two products. Do not draw one arrow that claims a native connector.

lessons.title: Salesforce starts as a CCP embed in a sandbox
outcomes: The softphone in the embed is the Connect CCP.
Sandbox first. Production is a later copy of a configuration you have already tried.
The page points at separate installation guides for Lightning and for Classic.
This room does not invent screen-pop fields. Read the adapter guide before you promise a pop.

lessons.title: AI agents: configure, cite, and a way out
outcomes: Every generated answer in a design review needs the article title.
Keep DTMF escape.
Do not send payment card data into a prompt.
Voice ID is not the fallback. It has ended.

lessons.title: CRM configuration and the faults that look like routing bugs
outcomes: Log the attribute in the flow and in the CRM activity.
Search profiles before creating a lead.
Outbound click-to-dial uses the queue caller ID.
Retest after every managed-package upgrade in a sandbox.

lessons.title: E911 for agents on the CCP
outcomes: CivicAddress is a JSON string, not a JSON object. The keys include country, A1, A3, HNO, RD, STS, and PC.
Prompt agents to confirm the address at the start of a shift if they roam.
This is not available as a transfer from a customer call.
Outside those Regions, do not invent a 911 design. Use the local emergency method and say so.

lessons.title: Future hooks, not future rewrites
outcomes: Prefer events over polling the real-time API.
Prefer attributes over asking the agent to retype.
Prefer a module for a policy that every future flow must share.
Re-read the quota before you promise a vendor a fan-out.

lessons.title: Glossary
outcomes: The glossary is also a flashcard deck.
Old-platform words are included on purpose.
Ended features stay in the glossary so people can see the date.
If a definition has no source, it does not belong here.

lessons.title: Third-party recorders and live media
outcomes: Streaming and S3 recording can both be on. Know which one the evaluator uses.
Stop the stream. Leaked streams cost money and keep audio you meant to end.
Do not stream calls that your policy says must not be recorded.
Test cross-account access with a security review, not with a long-lived access key.

lessons.title: Configure conversational analytics and fix the empty transcript
outcomes: A flow that sets recording off 'for this queue' also kills the transcript.
Rules on keywords need the real-time path.
Summaries are absent until the post-contact job finishes.
Chat analytics is a separate enablement from voice. It arrived later and is configured on the chat contact.

lessons.title: Integration maps
outcomes: ContactId joins contact-scoped tools.
Profile id joins customer-scoped tools.
Agent ARN or username joins WFM.
CivicAddress joins only the 911 whisper.

lessons.title: Mind map
outcomes: Telephony is not the CRM.
WFM is not the real-time board.
E911 is not the customer's caller ID.
Agent assist is not the system of record.

lessons.title: Quality management on top of analytics
outcomes: Calibrate reviewers on the same five contacts.
The transcript can miss a word. The audio decides.
Redaction must run before a reviewer who should not see the secret sees the form.
Coaching is a workflow. The form is not the coaching.

lessons.title: Recording and screen capture
outcomes: Customer and agent channels should be identifiable for QM.
KMS failures look like missing files.
A transfer to the PSTN ends Connect's recording of the far leg.
Retention is a lifecycle rule you write down.

lessons.title: Third-party WFM configuration and faults
outcomes: Give each consumer its own iterator.
Alarm on iterator age.
Map statuses in a reviewed table.
Do not send production events into a vendor lab account.

lessons.title: Native forecasting and scheduling
outcomes: You need history before the forecast is trustworthy.
Shrinkage is an input you own. The tool does not know your meetings.
Published schedules are what adherence compares against.
A queue with no staffable profile makes the forecast look 'wrong'.

lessons.title: The contact center is not the whole operation
outcomes: Every sister system must store ContactId or it cannot be audited.
Pick one system of record for the case.
Pick one adherence feed: agent events.
Pick one emergency design per kind of agent: desk phone or CCP.

lessons.title: Attributes are the only memory the next system gets
outcomes: System attributes include the queue, the channel, and the customer endpoint.
Lex exposes intent and slots. Copy the ones you care about into your own names.
A transfer to another flow keeps the contact attributes.
A transfer to a phone number leaves Connect. Attributes do not ride the PSTN.

lessons.title: The block catalog, grouped by job
outcomes: Check hours, Check queue status, Check staffing, and Get metrics are how a flow refuses work it cannot staff.
Set logging and Set recording are how you can prove what happened.
Show view is the step-by-step guide.
Agentic CX and Connect assistant are the 2026 AI entry points. Voice ID blocks remain on the list and should not be added. Support ended 20 May 2026.

lessons.title: Every error branch is a product decision
outcomes: Turn logging on before the first test call.
The disconnect flow does not save you from an error hang-up. The customer is already gone.
Wait and Play prompt are how you avoid silence during async Lambda.
Touchtone buffer lets callers type ahead. Turn it on only if the prompts allow it.

lessons.title: The flow language is how instances share a design
outcomes: Use the JSON to move a flow between a test instance and production.
Do not hand-edit a 2,000-line export without a diff.
Modules have their own JSON.
The API still says Amazon Connect in places. The admin guide may say Connect Customer. The JSON types are what the API accepts.

lessons.title: Modules are how you stop copying flows
outcomes: Publish, then invoke. A draft module is not what production runs.
Keep authentication, language selection, and recording policy in modules.
Version the module in your stack as ContactFlowModule JSON.
Test the module with the same error branches as a flow.

lessons.title: Flow types are not one canvas
outcomes: A customer queue flow is interruptible.
Transfer to queue inside a customer queue flow moves a contact that is already queued.
End flow / Resume ends the flow and does not hang up.
Disconnect hangs up.

lessons.title: Certifications and the badges that are not certifications
outcomes: Cloud Practitioner is the shared vocabulary of accounts, Regions, and billing.
AI Practitioner is context for generative features. It does not configure a flow.
The Communications Specialist badge covers telephony, IVR, flows, routing, and omnichannel.
A badge is issued through Credly within about two weeks of the knowledge check. It is not a proctored certification.

lessons.title: CloudWatch tells you the flow ran
outcomes: Logging can be turned off in the flow. Check that before you blame the log group.
A missing error in Lambda's log with an error in the flow log means Connect rejected the response before or without a completed invoke.
Metrics such as ConcurrentEmails belong in an alarm, not in a monthly slide.
Flow logs are not a recording and not a CTR.

lessons.title: IAM is not the security profile
outcomes: connect:StartOutboundVoiceContact and StartChatContact are privileged. Do not put them on a public web role.
profile and cases are separate IAM services.
wisdom is still the prefix you will see for agent assist in the service authorization reference.
Least privilege means the instance ARN, not Resource star, once the design is real.

lessons.title: Kinesis is how the ecosystem listens
outcomes: CTRs are near real time, not instant, and consumers must tolerate duplicates.
Only one Firehose is the default CTR delivery. Fan out by consuming a stream.
Join on ContactId. There is no other honest key.
Agent events are the adherence feed. Historical reports are not.

lessons.title: Lambda is a seam, not a place to hide a CRM
outcomes: Add the function to the instance. An identity policy alone does not let the flow invoke it.
Return a flat string map or JSON, matching the block. Nested objects fail a string-map block.
Log the ContactId. The flow log has no Lambda RequestId to join on.
Default block timeout is 3 seconds. Raise it on purpose, not by hoping.

lessons.title: The network path is part of the product
outcomes: The usual failure string names turn:TurnNlb and port 3478.
ice_collection_timeout means the browser never gathered candidates.
A custom CCP can be media-less, but then you still do not have a softphone.
Video adds a Chime subnet and does not support VDI.

lessons.title: Regions, endpoints, and why Osaka is special
outcomes: New accounts start at two instances per Region.
Quota raises are per Region. Raising Oregon does not raise Virginia.
The CCP domain is instance.my.connect.aws. The old awsapps.com domain is documented as going away.
Softphone TURN endpoints are Regional. A laptop in another country still talks to the instance Region.

lessons.title: S3 holds the proof
outcomes: Block public access. These objects are conversations.
KMS and the bucket policy are both required when you use a customer-managed key.
Attachment size defaults to 20 MB and can be set up to 100 MB.
Email has its own storage path through the email channel and Amazon SES networking guidance.

lessons.title: A depends-on map you can defend
outcomes: Read the depends-on line on each track before you skip ahead.
A migration bridge without flows and routing is a glossary, not a plan.
E911 depends on Profiles, Lambda, and an outbound whisper flow.
Price estimates depend on the rate card date, which this campus stamps as 14 October 2026.

lessons.title: Feature timeline
outcomes: 2020-07-23, Contact Lens generally available.
2026-04-28, the family announcement.
2026-05-20, Voice ID end of support.

lessons.title: What Connect actually depends on
outcomes: The family name Amazon Connect now covers Customer, Health, Decisions, and Talent. This campus teaches the contact center.
IAM prefixes you will meet include connect, profile, cases, wisdom, and voiceid. voiceid is historical after 20 May 2026.
The data plane for agents is the browser, not a PBX firmware image.
Shared responsibility: AWS runs the platform. You run flows, identity, keys, numbers, quotas, and the agent network.

lessons.title: Create the instance on purpose
outcomes: Default concurrent calls: 10. Request more before a pilot that is larger than a team.
Storage choices can be updated, but existing objects do not move themselves.
Two instances per Region is the starting quota.
CloudTrail records the control-plane calls. Turn it on in the account, not inside the flow.

lessons.title: CloudFormation, CDK, and Terraform
outcomes: CDK uses the same CloudFormation types.
Phone number resources can fail for quota reasons the template cannot see.
Do not put production flow JSON only in a laptop. The JSON is the source of truth the designer also edits, so pick one writer.
aws-samples and amazon-connect/amazon-connect-streams are the public code to read, not to paste into production unchanged.

lessons.title: SAML attributes that make a user real
outcomes: Test with one user and one profile before you federate the whole center.
Role session name problems show up as opaque access errors. Read the IdP logs and the Connect login error together.
Do not create a parallel local admin and forget it when people leave.
The replica instance needs the same identity story or failover signs nobody in.

lessons.title: Prompts, statuses, and the small quotas
outcomes: Name prompts for the flow that uses them.
Custom statuses feed WFM only if the WFM mapping knows the name.
Reports: 2000 per instance, and every saved personal report counts.
User hierarchy groups: 500 across all levels.

lessons.title: CUCM and Webex beside Connect
outcomes: Test the transfer in both directions.
Codec and DTMF on the CUCM side still matter after the transfer.
Caller ID from Connect must be a number CUCM's route plan accepts.
Document which system records the second leg.

lessons.title: Salesforce: CTI Adapter and SCC-AC
outcomes: One system of record for the case.
The serverless app has an IAM role. Review it.
Sandbox, then production.
Test outbound click-to-dial. It uses the caller ID rules.

lessons.title: ServiceNow Voice
outcomes: A 5-second hold file is a hard constraint in that guide. Do not upload a 30-second loop and wonder.
Map queues by name in a table you review.
The placeholder phone channel is not a real number.
Test transfer flows. They are shared with ITSM in the guide's description.

lessons.title: Teams is a chat client in the published pattern
outcomes: Do not describe this blog as 'Connect telephony inside Teams'.
The Lambda is yours to secure.
Typing indicators and session lookup are application code.
Voice and chat are different projects. Staff them separately.

lessons.title: When the work is slower than eight seconds
outcomes: Tell the caller what is happening.
A timeout branch still needs a prompt.
Long work belongs in a queue or a task, not in the greet flow.
Measure duration in CloudWatch before you argue about the flow.

lessons.title: The response contract
outcomes: Idempotent writes. Retries happen.
Timeouts in the Lambda console must be higher than the block timeout or you will add a second failure mode.
Cold starts count against the 8 seconds.
Secrets stay in the function environment or in Secrets Manager, not in flow attributes.

lessons.title: Association, resource policy, and the log that says AccessDenied
outcomes: Use an alias, not $LATEST, in production.
Resource-based policy and identity policy answer different questions.
VPC-attached functions need a path to their dependency and still must return in time.
Terraform's association resource is the reviewable form of the console click.

lessons.title: Evaluation forms, from a blank page to a rule
outcomes: Sample forms cover agent-handled and self-service interactions.
The page names five outcome metrics on sample forms: customer satisfaction, churn propensity, successful sale, and full or partial self-service success.
A PDF import comes back as a draft, typically within one minute, for you to review.
You can save a draft and leave. Activation is a later step, after preview and validation.

lessons.title: Turn conversational analytics on for the contact
outcomes: A transfer creates another contact ID. Add the block again. A queue-to-queue transfer copies the configuration.
With several analytics blocks, real-time uses the first. Post-call agent analytics uses the last.
From October 2026, automated-interaction analytics moves toward real-time and uses the first block. The page says Customer Basic instances stay on post-contact analytics using the last block.
Sentiment starts on when the language supports it. Redaction can miss sensitive data. The page says it is not a HIPAA de-identification.

lessons.title: Fallback is a route, not a failure
outcomes: Timeout and error are different from fallback. Connect them separately.
A DTMF escape key should exist even in a speech bot.
Test with noise, with silence, and with an accent the bot has not heard.
Do not send fallback into another bot with no exit.

lessons.title: Get customer input is the Lex block
outcomes: Branch on the intent name you configured, not on the sentence the caller said.
Slots are empty when the caller hangs up mid-prompt. Handle that.
DTMF and speech can both fill a slot. Test both.
A fallback intent should reach a person or a callback.

lessons.title: Slots become attributes or they vanish
outcomes: Validate the account id in Lambda. Do not trust a spoken string as authorization.
Barge-in and touchtone buffering change what the caller can interrupt.
Log the intent and the confidence behavior you actually configured.
Keep the bot alias stable. Pointing production at a draft alias is how Friday breaks.

lessons.title: Cases survive the transfer
outcomes: Related items default to 200. Files on a case default to 50.
A template with 50 custom fields is the ceiling and it is not adjustable.
Status values are a contract with the CRM if both systems have a case. Pick one system of record.
Closing a contact does not close a case unless you said so.

lessons.title: One customer, three objects
outcomes: Search before create, or you duplicate people.
A task can attach to the same case.
Deletes and merges are identity-resolution events. Tell the CRM.
Retention of profile objects is a privacy decision. The quota allows a long expiry. Your policy may not.

lessons.title: Profiles are the customer, not the contact
outcomes: Keys on an object type default to 10.
A profile object maxes at 250 KB in the quota table. All objects on one profile share a larger cap.
Calculated attributes and event triggers have their own quotas.
E911 addresses for agents are stored here on purpose. That is a different profile population from customers. Do not mix the matching rules carelessly.

lessons.title: Tasks are the channel with no audio
outcomes: Task templates: 50 per instance, not adjustable, with 50 custom fields.
A task flow can still call Lambda.
Do not use a voice queue for work that has no call.
Expiry and assignment are visible in metrics. Alarm on age.

lessons.title: What a failover drill has to prove
outcomes: Write the expected caller experience during the shift.
Include the IdP endpoint in the firewall test.
Measure the Osaka delay if that is your pair. Do not discover it in an incident.
Rollback is a shift back, and you should time it.

lessons.title: Migration patterns that survive contact with a Monday
outcomes: Reports will not match on day one if the old AHT included something yours does not. Write both formulas.
Agents need the CCP network before the port, not after.
Keep the old recording system until the new object's retention is proven.
One number is a test. A range is a decision.

lessons.title: Only one multi-Region design is supported
outcomes: Identity has to work in both Regions.
A Lambda in the flow must exist in both Regions.
Osaka delivery can take up to 20 seconds.
Shift 10 percent first. Do not start at 100.

lessons.title: Routing criteria, expiry, and a preferred agent
outcomes: An AND step can use up to eight attributes. An OR step can use up to three conditions, and only when you set the criteria dynamically.
NOT is also dynamic only. OR sits at the top. AND can sit inside OR.
Each step needs a timer. The last step may be set never to expire.
A very short DurationInSeconds can let ordinary queue routing compete with the proficiency step.

lessons.title: Hours and overrides
outcomes: Check hours before Set working queue.
Publish the time zone in the prompt if you serve more than one.
Overnight hours that cross midnight need a careful read of the day boundary.
The override quota is not adjustable.

lessons.title: Priority, delay, and concurrency
outcomes: Delay is in seconds. A delay of 0 means eligible immediately.
Two profiles can point at one queue with different priority.
Cross-channel concurrency is a choice. A voice call plus three chats is a workload, not a free feature.
Change routing priority / age if a flow must jump the line. Use it rarely and log why.

lessons.title: Queues wait. Profiles decide who is eligible.
outcomes: Priority is per profile, not a property of the queue alone.
A contact can sit in a queue that is outside the hours if you never checked hours.
Callbacks still occupy the queue's logic. They need a staffed profile.
Name queues for the work, not for a person.

lessons.title: Quick connects and the flows behind them
outcomes: Put the quick connect on the queue the agent is actually using.
The transfer flow should set recording if the destination is still inside Connect.
External numbers need a spoken confirmation if the destination is a mobile.
Interrupt agent is the rare tool for forcing a specific agent. It is not the everyday quick connect.

lessons.title: Proficiencies filter inside a queue
outcomes: Proficiency routing is documented for voice, chat, task, and email.
AND and OR are the Boolean operators. Comparison is >=, or a range of levels from 1 to 5.
The same attribute cannot appear more than once in one expression.
A custom predefined-attribute name cannot start with aws: or connect:.

lessons.title: Encryption is a key policy
outcomes: Test a recording end to end after you change the key.
A replica Region needs a key strategy you have actually written down.
Do not use the same key for recordings and for unrelated application secrets if your blast radius matters.
Access to the bucket and access to the key are both required to listen.

lessons.title: How to talk about the price without inventing it
outcomes: Say which product form you priced.
A 7-minute call is not 7 times a rounded minute if the voice charge is per second. Telephony in the example still has a 60 second minimum.
The estimator in the lab stamps the date on every result.
Seats are not the unit. There is no seat license in this rate card.

lessons.title: Quotas are a project plan
outcomes: Alarm at 80 percent.
Account-level quotas and resource-level quotas raise differently.
CLI 2.13.20 or newer is required for some resource-level quota calls.
Campaign concurrency and external voice connectors start at 0.

lessons.title: SAML, least privilege, and the admin you forgot
outcomes: Review security profiles when someone changes jobs.
Recording access is a security profile permission. Treat it like access to the conversation, because it is.
CloudTrail the control plane.
Global Resiliency sign-in uses an extra endpoint. The IdP and the firewall both need it.

lessons.title: Claiming and the false 'limit' on the first number
outcomes: Raise the call concurrency quota before you publish the number.
Associate the number with a flow or the caller hears nothing useful.
For Global Resiliency, numbers join a traffic distribution group.
Write down the carrier and the country. Porting later depends on both.

lessons.title: SIP, external voice, and what is not a trunk in the CUCM sense
outcomes: Do not design a SIP trunk in CUCM and assume Connect will register to it as a phone.
One-way audio after a transfer is often the other system's codec or network, not the CCP.
External voice is for analytics on audio you already have.
Campaign answering-machine detection is Check call progress, and only in campaign flows.

lessons.title: Outbound calls and caller ID
outcomes: StartOutboundVoiceContact is an API. Guard it.
An outbound whisper flow runs before the customer and agent join. Recording for outbound is set there.
Call phone number is the block that dials from an outbound whisper flow.
Country allow lists block destinations even when the flow is correct.

lessons.title: Porting without losing the rollback
outcomes: Match the caller ID and any CNAM story you actually have. Do not promise caller-name display the product does not set.
Internal extensions can stay on CUCM. Only the public number has to move.
Update the CRM screen pop to the new ContactId in the same window.
Tell the WFM and recording tools the storage path before the port, or the first day has no recordings in the old tool.

lessons.title: DID, toll-free, shared cost, UIFN
outcomes: DID is one carrier. It presents a local number. It is not load-balanced across carriers.
You can mix DID and toll-free on one instance.
Inbound telephony in the example is charged per minute with a 60 second minimum.
Voice service is a second charge, 0.038 or 0.018 USD per minute depending on the product form, billed per second with a 10 second minimum.

lessons.title: Audio quality is a path, not a codec myth
outcomes: Stateless firewalls drop the return UDP.
VDI relocates the media.
A bad headset is still possible. Swap it after the network test, not before.
Packet captures are the capture step, not the first step.

lessons.title: Faults worth memorizing
outcomes: SAML users with no routing profile signed in and cannot take work.
Global Resiliency numbers missing from the replica were never in a distribution group.
A recording missing from S3 is policy, key, or the block.
CTR delay under five minutes is buffering. Past that, check Firehose errors.

lessons.title: A flow log you can actually search
outcomes: Turn logging on in a module if every flow should log.
Retention of the log group is your setting.
PII in attributes will land in the log. Do not log secrets.
A successful block with a wrong branch is not an error. Read the attributes.

lessons.title: Leg, id, counter, capture
outcomes: A flow log error with no Lambda log is a permission or a payload rejection.
A CCP error that names TurnNlb is the network, even if the flow is perfect.
A fast busy on a campaign is the zero quota until proven otherwise.
A missing recording is the block, the bucket, or the key.

lessons.title: Hiring plans and scheduling plans
outcomes: Create a scenario before you create the plan.
Shrinkage and available full-time equivalents can be imported. Hiring plans use day-level files. Scheduling plans use interval-level files.
Task and email plans can start from an automatic backlog when you use an average time to complete.
The getting-started list ends with review, then publish. Override and re-run are for hiring plans.

lessons.title: The forecast interval is a one-time choice
outcomes: The first short-term or long-term forecast is typically ready within 4 hours, and often in about 1 hour.
Only the newest forecast stays on the page. Download a copy if you need to keep that day.
The forecasting page lists the order: interval, forecast groups, historical import, create, inspect, publish.
A change to the forecast group, such as adding or removing a queue, starts that computation again.

lessons.title: Publish the schedule before you talk about adherence
outcomes: Forecasts update on their own. Publishing is the step that hands one to schedulers.
Short-term forecasts feed scheduling, up to 18 weeks ahead.
Long-term forecasts feed capacity planning, up to 64 weeks ahead.
The overview names administrator, forecaster, scheduler, capacity planner, and agent as the people in the workflow.

lessons.title: The CCP is a web app with a telephone inside
outcomes: Supported browsers only. A locked-down browser without WebRTC permissions fails closed.
Headsets with their own DSP can still be fine. Browser permission for the microphone is not optional.
The Endpoint Connectivity tool is the first test, before a packet capture.
Stateless firewalls need ephemeral UDP back in.

lessons.title: Streams is the supported way to embed the CCP
outcomes: Init once. A second init on navigation is a classic bug.
Destroy the session on sign-out.
Do not store the agent's password in your app. Use SAML.
Media still needs UDP 3478. The library does not tunnel it.

lessons.title: VDI, VPN, and the audio path
outcomes: One-way audio is often NAT or a stateful rule that never saw the return traffic.
Jitter and loss show up as robotic audio, not as a flow error.
Do not stack a VPN, a proxy, and VDI and then tune the flow.
Remote agents need the same allow list as the office.

lessons.title: The workspace is where the ecosystem becomes visible
outcomes: Give agents one place to see the attribute you collected.
Views are configuration, not a custom CCP.
A custom CCP using Streams is justified when the workspace cannot host the system of record.
ACW is part of the handle time the WFM tool must see.
